title: Creme Brulee
subtitle: Classic French baked cream custard
excerpt: Rich vanilla custard baked in ramekins and finished with a layer of caramelised sugar. The contrast between the crackable caramel top and the cold, silky cream below is the whole point.

recipe.sourceNotes: Creme brulee (burnt cream) in its modern form is associated with French and British fine dining of the twentieth century, though closely related dishes appear much earlier in European cookbooks. Cambridge burnt cream and a similar dish in a 1691 French recipe are often cited as precursors.

recipeTools.notes: For caramelising the sugar. A grill can be used but a blowtorch gives a better result.

content.text: Creme brulee is a baked vanilla cream custard in individual ramekins, finished with a thin layer of sugar that is caramelised to a crisp, glassy top. The custard is made with just cream, egg yolks, sugar, and vanilla, baked in a bain-marie so it sets gently and evenly. It must be completely cold before you add the sugar and brulee it.
Heat the oven to 150 C / fan 130 C / gas 2. Place four 150 ml ramekins in a deep roasting tin.
Heat the cream and vanilla pod and seeds in a small saucepan over a medium heat until steaming, just below simmering. Remove from the heat.

Whisk the egg yolks and 75 g caster sugar together in a bowl until pale. Pour the warm cream into the yolk mixture slowly, whisking constantly. Strain through a fine sieve into a jug. Skim off any bubbles.

Pour the custard evenly into the ramekins. Pour enough boiling water into the roasting tin to reach halfway up the sides of the ramekins. Cover loosely with foil and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the custard is just set with a very slight wobble in the centre.
Lift the ramekins from the bain-marie and leave to cool, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight until very cold.

When ready to serve, sprinkle a tablespoon of caster sugar evenly over each custard. Use a blowtorch to melt and caramelise the sugar in a circular motion until it is a deep amber and glass-hard. Leave for 1 minute before serving so the caramel sets firm.
